log.text: Gemini 4 Neon started judging against Asaf's checklist.
Analyzing the Media Content

I am now meticulously reviewing the video and audio, cross-referencing everything against the QA checklist and the original intent. The video's duration is 4.04 seconds, with a 1920x1080 resolution. The audio reveals Marcus saying "Start today" at the very beginning; his voice has a warm, friendly, Midwestern American quality.
Examining the Visuals

I'm now diving deep into the visual details, specifically the interaction between Marcus and MILA. My focus is on MILA's placement relative to Marcus's arm, especially around the 0:00-0:01 mark. The initial impression of MILA standing on his forearm is challenged; there's a hovering effect that needs further scrutiny. I'm noting Marcus's right arm's movement as it interacts with the folder.
Scrutinizing the Floating Violation

I'm now zeroing in on the floating violation between 0:02 and 0:04. MILA's shoes clearly detach from Marcus's forearm and hover, making this a "grounded on a surface (never floating)" violation. I'm focusing on the visual cues—the background peeking through and the precise angle—to determine the best way to flag this critical detail.
Investigating Movement Dynamics

I'm now deeply engaged in the motion analysis, focusing specifically on MILA's hand and arm movements. The blue folder interaction at the start is key. I've re-evaluated the initial push and subsequent gliding. Her arm positions at 0:02-0:03, waving with one hand and the other on her hip, require precise analysis. Further, I am confirming MILA's hand is not holding anything on her hip as well as o
pening her mouth to show her teeth, not keeping it closed as intended.
Assessing the Folder's Details

I am now focusing on the blue folder details, specifically the text and size changes. "M.I.L. Cleaners / Franchise Info" appears on the folder, though it is small and somewhat blurry. Crucially, I see that the folder changes size and proportions significantly from 0:00 to 0:02, which is notable. It shrinks and morphs when moved to Marcus's chest; this aspect ratio change is significant.
Observing the Details

I'm now zeroing in on the finer points, I've noted the white label on the blue folder—its size and text clarity change from the beginning to the 0:02 mark. The shirt logo on Marcus's chest also shifts subtly as the folder moves. I'm focusing on Marcus's left arm, held rigidly and unnaturally under the van door handle for the entire clip, which raises many questions. And I am cross-referencing this
against his right arm which is at his side initially.
Evaluating the Frame's Position

I am now assessing the framing and Marcus's positioning. My analysis reveals that his face is significantly left of the center 9:16 column; cropping would cut off a portion of his face and body. The lip-sync analysis confirms good synchronization with "Start today," and his mouth remains closed afterward. I am cross-referencing this against the camera placement for conformity.
Pinpointing the Frame's Details

I've just pinpointed MILA's position, at roughly 46%-60% of the frame, inside the center 9:16, while the folder starts at 54%-68%, moving to Marcus's chest at 25%-43%—a clear framing violation. The static camera lacks any dynamic movement; the "whoosh" sound is soft and limited, failing to be a strong "hook." I see significant floating with MILA's shoes clearly separated from Marcus's forearm and
the blue folder scales and text changing as well! Also, I have begun to evaluate MILA's hands and actions.
Reviewing Acting Dynamics

I'm now zeroing in on MILA and Marcus's performance. MILA's movements—pushing the folder, waving, holding still—are acceptable, though her stationary pose is unnaturally long. Marcus's left arm, rigidly positioned under the door handle throughout, looks unmotivated and unnatural once MILA begins floating. This raises questions about the overall performance.
Confirming Final Fails

I am now consolidating all failure points into the schema for final review, confirming MILA's floating, the prop's fluctuating scale/clarity, the framing violation, the static camera, and Marcus's unnatural pose. I'm ensuring everything is accounted for, using only verdict, fails, passes, and usable range. I have also verified all other aspects as passing.

Verdict FAIL. 0:00-0:04 MILA grounding: MILA floats above Marcus's forearm with visible van gap under her shoes instead of standing grounded. | 0:00-0:02 Prop size and text stability (Items 4, 23): Blue folder noticeably shrinks while sliding to Marcus's chest, and its label text appears soft/slightly garbled. | 0:00-0:04 Framing / 9:16 safe area (Item 19): Marcus's face and the held folder sit le
ft of the center 9:16 column and would be cut off in vertical crops. | 0:00-0:02 Hook / camera motion (Item 2): Camera stays nearly static with no dynamic hook move in the opening seconds.
Gemini 4 Neon started judging against Asaf's checklist.
Analyzing System Requirements

I'm currently dissecting the system prompt's constraints. I've noted the strict JSON formatting requirement, specifically the need for string values to be double-quoted. Also, that only scalars, boolean and null are permitted. I'm focusing on the intricacies and ensuring my approach aligns perfectly with the specified output demands.
Refining Output Constraints

I'm now zeroing in on the output specifics, taking care to avoid any extraneous comments or text outside the JSON block, as requested. I've also integrated the verbosity reduction directive for long-form attributes, ensuring brevity and prioritization of summaries over granular details. The schema is embedded, and I am watching the clip! I am watching the details of the clip.
Observing Mila's Features

I'm now focused on Mila's visual characteristics within the specified timeframe. I've noted her 2D cartoon style, matching the model sheet details: gray curly hair, pink glasses, pearl necklace, blue polka dot dress, pink apron, yellow gloves, and blue shoes. I am watching for subtle details, specifically, the movement of her hands, mouth and eyes, as they may suggest more clues. I am watching her
hands clap, wave, and wiggle, and have found that she always has two arms and two hands visible.
Tracing the Red Line

I'm now deeply immersed in the circle's creation (0:00-0:03). The marker's orientation is crucial: at 0:00.5, it initially tilts right, the red line emerging counter-clockwise. However, the marker tip's position relative to the line is intriguing, as the tip remains static. The marker pivots back, and I'm tracing the movement with precision.
Dissecting the Movement

I'm now zeroing in on the marker's path during the oval creation. The animation breaks at 0:01.5, showing that the marker tip is near "YOUR" but the oval inexplicably finishes drawing independently of it. I'm noting the clear violation of the expected cause-and-effect continuity. I'm also examining MILA's hand movements, which are also inconsistent with how the oval is drawn.
Investigating the Text

I'm now investigating potential text morphing within the video. I've compiled a list of street names and their positions on the map, particularly focusing on those near MILA. I noticed a crucial shift at 0:02; "Orn Rd" or similar gibberish suddenly appears near her hair, where previously there was only a street! "Maple St" on the left also shows an interesting evolution as her arm/marker moves.
Examining the Text's Changes

I'm now zeroing in on the text's behavior throughout the animation. I'm focusing on "Maple St" and how it changes at the end. I noted a fascinating morph at 0:02 of garbled text (likely "Orn Rd"), followed by a brief partial occlusion. "Oak Ave" also seems to wobble slightly as the marker crosses it. It is clear there are multiple instances of the same street name. "YOUR TERRITORY" is partially co
vered but stable. Also, I've observed that key elements remain within the 9:16 column.
Assessing the Framing

I'm now zeroing in on the implications of the 9:16 crop. Analyzing the 1920x1080 frame, I see that MILA is mostly outside the critical 9:16 central column, which means any crop would severely cut her off. Even "YOUR TERRITORY" and the red oval extend outside this key area, confirming a cropping failure. Additionally, the hands on the map are static, and MILA's open-toothed smile throughout the cli
p contradicts the stated intent of her mouth being closed.
Verifying the Character

I'm now comparing MILA's appearance in the video to the reference image. She's a perfect match to the 2D model, staying flat, with a soft drop shadow. I've confirmed her eyes are both open and that she has her yellow gloves on. I'm noting the static camera and that there's no real push-in. I'm also confirming that MILA's outfit matches the reference image.

Initiating QA Protocol

I'm ready to dive into the QA evaluation of the "MILA" video clip. I'll meticulously assess the 4.04s video, focusing on the franchise-recruitment ad's effectiveness, keeping the 2D cartoon grandma as the focal point. My analysis will center ratings to avoid extremes. The final output will be a clean, valid JSON file.
Refining Assessment Criteria

Now, I'm adjusting my approach based on the direct PASS/FAIL requirement. Numeric scoring is unnecessary; I'll streamline the JSON output. I'm also reducing detail and verbosity, prioritizing brief, high-level summaries for descriptive elements. My focus is on frame-by-frame analysis, starting with the opening scene and MILA's initial appearance and anatomy. I'll meticulously evaluate her visual a
ttributes and actions.
Analyzing MILA's Movements

I'm deep into examining MILA's movements in detail, particularly from 00:00 to 00:04. The way she bends and places the sticky note is really giving me pause. I'm focusing on the animation's visual consistency, and am concerned about the significant anatomical distortions I'm observing in her dress and arm proportions. Her hands and size also seem inconsistent. I'm noting specific frame times.
Observing Camera & MILA

I'm now focusing on the camera's gradual zoom and MILA's corresponding appearance. Her eyes remain consistently open, and her smile is static, although her head gets comparatively much larger. Her position, as she stands on the table, creates an unusual, almost pasted-on effect due to the top-down perspective, but it's acceptable for the 2D style. I'm also examining Marcus's hand movement in the s
hot.
Evaluating Audio & Visual

I'm now focusing on the audio and its match to the visuals. The male voice is warm and clear, with no issues in delivery. I've listened closely to the SFX around the sticky note placement, confirming that there is no distinct "paper stick" sound, though there is faint music that may resemble it. I'm verifying the visual consistency of the sticky note text with the spoken words, and note the matchi
ng of key phrases.
Assessing Text & Framing

I'm now deeply engaged in a text and framing check. The sticky notes display "LOCAL MARKETING", "ONGOING GUIDANCE", and "TRAINING" as requested; all are legible, and correctly spelled. I've noted that their placement within the frame is slightly off, however, with "LOCAL MARKETING" appearing to the left, and "TRAINING" to the right, which creates a slight issue in the center 9:16 crop.
Reviewing Visual Anomalies

I'm now zeroing in on the specific visual issues. The framing cuts off a significant portion of the scene (Item 19), with MILA at 75% on the right and partially cut off. Her anatomy (Items 17 & 25) is clearly distorted from 00:01.5 to 00:04.0, particularly the dress's arch-like loops and the unnaturally stretched forearms. Additionally, from 00:00 to 00:01.5, MILA's movement down the table lacks n
atural perspective, and her feet disappear. However, I confirmed Item 2 (hook) isn't directly applicable here.

Analyzing the Video's Details

I'm meticulously reviewing the video clip, cross-referencing every nuance against the prompt and checklist. I've noted the ~4-second duration, 1920x1080 resolution, and the intended audio: a male voice speaking the phrase "You still run it: hiring, quoting, leading." I'm doing a detailed audio check for accuracy and clarity.
Assessing the Visuals

I've got a good grasp of the audio's characteristics: calm, friendly male voice, Midwestern accent. Now, I'm diving into the visuals, focusing on Marcus. The gentle camera dolly-in is smooth. He's at the kitchen table, phone to ear, writing. His mouth stays closed. The "MIL Cleaners" shirt text is slightly unclear, and the notepad scribbles are intentionally illegible AI-generated text, which is g
ood.
Scrutinizing MILA's Details

I'm now laser-focused on MILA, the animated character, scrutinizing her presentation frame by frame. I've noted that her notepad, thankfully, has no real, legible content, and the text is appropriately garbled/illegible. However, I've just observed that MILA seems a 3D figurine/clay/plastic toy. Her 3D lighting/shading seems quite obvious. I'm checking her animation. Her mouth is clearly opening w
ide, with slight lip movement, as she gives two thumbs up.
Identifying the Flaws

I've hit a snag with MILA. The prompt's "mouth closed" directive is violated—her mouth *clearly* opens at 0:02-0:03. Moreover, the 3D-rendered appearance with obvious lighting/shading violates Item 25. And regarding her hands: the thumbs up look awkward, and her hands at 0:02.5-0:04, are not the right shape. I can confidently conclude that at 0:03-0:04 she gives two thumbs up, one hand per side. T
his is all clearly non-compliant.
Verifying the Visuals

I've just assessed MILA's eye and framing details, confirming both eyes remain open, so Item 12 is compliant. However, my framing analysis is revealing a significant issue with Item 19. It seems MILA's position places her *outside* the center 9:16 column, which means she'd be partially cut off in a 9:16 crop. Marcus's head is centered! I'm now double-checking the horizontal positioning to confirm
these observations and quantify the degree of non-compliance.

"update": "**Calculating Positioning and Issues**\n\nI've calculated MILA's horizontal position within the frame and confirmed she falls outside the central 9:16 column, which would cause her to be partially cropped. Further verification reveals the \"MIL Cleaners\" shirt text is garbled, and MILA's mouth opens violating the \"mouth closed\" directive. Her 3D rendering and lack of hook SFX also po
se non-compliance issues."
Summarizing the Compliance

I've distilled the compliance review into key PASS and FAIL categories. The script and Marcus's voice are accurate, and MILA keeps both eyes open. However, the notepad and shirt text are illegible, MILA renders as a 3D model, her mouth opens when it shouldn't, and her positioning exceeds the safe 9:16 frame.
